title: Choose valid clause boundaries
instructions: Select both revisions that correctly join the two independent clauses without changing their contrast.

parts.prompt: Base ideas: “The library was closing. Hana still needed one source.” Which TWO revisions are correct?

options.text: The library was closing, but Hana still needed one source.
The library was closing; Hana still needed one source.
The library was closing, Hana still needed one source.
Although the library was closing. Hana still needed one source.

choice_rationales.A: The comma and but form a valid boundary and make the contrast explicit.
choice_rationales.B: The semicolon correctly separates the closely related independent clauses.
choice_rationales.C: A comma alone creates a comma splice between the independent clauses.
choice_rationales.D: Although makes the first group dependent, so the full stop leaves a fragment.

parts.hint: Two independent clauses may be joined by a semicolon or by a comma plus a coordinating conjunction.
parts.correct_explanation: Both the comma-plus-but revision and the semicolon revision create valid boundaries while preserving the contrast.
